questions.stem: This question asks the reader to use “Explain measure length / Beats times beat unit. / The beat and the measure in simple meter”. Which option results?

answer.exemplar: Measure length equals beats per measure times beat-unit value, so a 4/4 measure lasts four quarter-note beats.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: beat count times unit value gives length. On that basis "Measure length equals beats per measure times beat-unit value, so a 4/4 measure lasts four…" is the supported choice.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The length of a dotted eighth

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about the length of a dotted eighth. dotted quarter is 1.5 quarters, dotted eighth is 0.75 quarters. A marginal reminder adds: compare quarter values. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: The standard for this item is “Compare dotted eighth values / Compare quarter values. / The length of a dotted eighth”. Which option meets the standard?

options.misconception: misjudges values
treats "They are equal" as if it followed from the evidence
confuses with tempo

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: dotted quarter is 1.5 quarters, dotted eighth is 0.75 quarters. On that basis "The dotted quarter is longer" is the supported choice. Option A ("The dotted eighth is longer") fails because it misjudges values; Option C ("They are equal") fails because it treats "They are equal" as if it followed from the evidence; Option D ("Cannot compare") fails because it confuses with tempo.
